newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares ease on politics, high o/n rates.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares ease on politics, high o/n rates.

text.p: Istanbul shares ended slightly lower amid political worries and overnight interest rates which remained high on Friday, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 2,004, down 12 points, or 0.6 percent from Thursday. It dropped 1.76 percent this week compared to last week's 3.4 percent jump.
Daily volume fell to 19.58 trillion lira ($120 million), from Thursday's 21.8 trillion ($133 million).

Toygar Sungur from Meksa Securities said the bearish sentiment which emerged in the afternoon session was partly due to the rejection of an article during a parliamentary debate on a bill to raise compulsory education to eight years from five.

Four articles of the bill were accepted since Thursday in the debate seen as the latest stage in the political fight between the new secularist government and the former ruling Islamists and their conservative allies.
Brokers said high overnight money and repo rates continued to block cash entry to the market.

The shortage prompted by hefty public sector salary payments and money demand ahead of the weekend caused overnight money and repo rates to keep their high levels and prompted heavy central bank funding on Friday.

"I think the bourse will wait for the results of the Treasury's first ever reverse t-bill auction on Monday. This may ease the liqudity shortage in the money market," Ibrahim Usul from Sahin Securities said.
The Treasury will open its first reverse auction to buy back bills due to mature on December 10. There are 380 trillion lira of outstanding December 10 bills in the market.
